title: Root-N Fluctuation State Evolution for Experiments under Causal Message Passing
banked_reason: D0.5.G: paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.2; fixed-horizon homogeneous Gaussian regular-interior CFSE is sound but below the field novelty floor, with no bounded in-scope change that raises the tier.
gap_reasons: The load-bearing adaptive-linearization proof remains too compressed at its delicate point: it introduces an unspecified finite collection of integrands and asserts a common b_N D_{N,t}^2 bound without explicitly deriving the recursive envelope products and uniform second-order remainder bounds.
The package supplies only an affine algebraic witness, not the advertised nonlinear early-kill simulation or a reproducible implementation check against the public CFEEstimator.
The narrow model scope, abbreviated core remainder argument, and limited practical evidence cap the projected leading-journal score despite the field-level joint CLT and inference result.

The declared Z^\circ variables are independent of primitive rows but not of G; the claimed conditional-iid Gaussian kernel is therefore not entailed (declare them fresh and independent of G, or formulate the bridge on an independent extension).
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery repaired the deleted-pivot nonregularity by restricting the theorem to uniformly all-active open families, established an explicit finite-N reused-G bridge and an adaptive-linearization theorem, and audited the affine T=3 witness with q=(1/2,85/64,159/128), determinant 10191/8192, and reuse covariance 7/32. The final package remained below the field floor because its homogeneous fixed-T scope and compressed uniform remainder proof capped the score at 6.8; the fresh auxiliary-Gaussian independence declaration and related-work relevance also remain local repair debt.
tldr: A fixed-horizon randomized experiment under homogeneous Causal-MP has a root-\(N\) fluctuation state evolution even though one unobserved Gaussian interaction matrix is reused at every date. An exact finite-\(N\) bridge conditions on the full observed past and uses empirical Gram projections to couple the reused-matrix fields to the auxiliary Gaussian-residual recursion. The theorem is uniform over an explicitly typed compact family \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal Q_T\) under named common moment, identification, rank, overlap, Gram, and Schur-residual margins. A single joint Gaussian experiment combines the differentiated mean, energy, Gram, and score moments with the initial-row empirical process. Its structural loading gives a direct asymptotic-linear representation for the all-treated-minus-none-treated path, and observable row contributions estimate the same covariance used by simultaneous Gaussian-max bands.
gap: Causal-MP supplies first-order state evolution, consistent total-treatment-effect estimation, and heuristic intervals, but no root-\(N\) law for empirical means, second moments, or scores under reuse of one latent matrix.
fill: Establish the finite-\(N\) conditional bridge with empirical Gram coefficients, construct the ordered auxiliary recursion and its ordinary derivative on the all-active interior, prove the expansion uniformly on compact \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal Q_T\), derive one joint moment--initial-law Gaussian experiment, map it through the structural and counterfactual derivatives, and calibrate an observable simultaneous path band from plug-in estimates of the same row influence.
